source_question: Suppose $A=(a_{jk})_{j,k=1}^n$ is a symmetric complex-valued matrix, meaning $a_{jk}=a_{kj}$ for all $j,k=1,\dotsc,n$. Given any two linearly independent vectors $\alpha=(\alpha^j)_{j=1}^n, \beta=(\beta^j)_{j=1}^n \in \mathbb{C}^n$ that satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^n(\alpha^j)^2=\sum_{j=1}^n(\beta^j)^2 =0$, it holds that $A(\alpha,\beta)=0$. Does it follow that $A=0$?
